claims.text: The dynamic mechanical behavior of HEAs is primarily governed by interactions between dislocations and severe lattice distortions.
Atomic-size mismatches cause severe lattice distortions in HEAs.
Dislocation interactions with severe lattice distortions enhance strain hardening.
Dislocation interactions with severe lattice distortions delay necking under dynamic loading.
Standard processing conditions will produce a homogeneous, single-phase HEA solid solution.
Severe lattice distortions create a rugged energy landscape for dislocation motion.
The rugged energy landscape increases resistance to dislocation glide.
Increased resistance to dislocation glide promotes strain hardening.
The proposed mechanism delays the onset of necking.
The proposed mechanism enhances ductility under dynamic loading.
Under identical dynamic loading, the HEA will have a higher strain-hardening rate than a simpler baseline alloy with lower lattice distortion.
Under identical dynamic loading, the HEA will have greater elongation to failure than the baseline alloy.
The hypothesis is expected to hold for single-phase solid-solution HEAs with significant atomic-size mismatch at room temperature and strain rates of 10^2 to 10^4 s^-1.
The hypothesis may not apply to HEAs containing significant secondary phases.
The hypothesis may not apply at very low or very high temperatures.
Grain-boundary effects or phase transformations may also influence the dynamic mechanical behavior of HEAs.
Failure to observe both higher strain-hardening rates and greater elongation to failure in the HEA relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe significant dislocation interactions with lattice distortions would falsify the hypothesis.
